Hi Anna / Acme team — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Scope: You’re evaluating Redwood for chat and retrieval use cases across support and sales assistant flows.
- Data concerns raised: PII handling, retention windows for request/response logs, fine-grained logging controls, and data residency (must remain in us-east-1).
- Redwood defaults: by default we use non-identifiable telemetry to improve our models and platform; customers who require it can opt out of training-on-customer-data and have explicit contractual language.

Action items I promised to follow up on: 
1) Confirm how to capture Acme’s formal opt-out for training/on-customer-data (see attached training_optout_form.pdf).
2) Share a summary of our logging/retention controls and the DPA amendment for signatures.
3) Note your residency requirement and any additional compliance docs you need.

Can you confirm that Acme would like to opt out of training-on-customer-data? If so, a reply confirming the opt-out or a signed copy of the attached form is sufficient — alternatively we can route a DPA amendment via DocuSign.

I’ve attached a short training opt-out form and our standard DPA for reference. I’ll loop in Marissa from Legal/Contracts and Dylan from Security to pick up the procurement and controls details.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- Acme confirms we will opt out of any training-on-customer-data / model improvement usage of our content. Please consider this our formal opt-out.
- Data residency: we require all production customer data and logs to be stored and processed in us-east-1 only.
- Retention: we prefer logs be retained 90 days by default; please include details in the amendment.

I’ve attached the completed training_optout_form.pdf and our procurement team (procurement@acmeinc.com) is copied for next steps on contracting. Please send the DPA amendment via DocuSign so procurement can sign.
